title: Evaluation of AI-supported motivational feedback in KEN-Online: A pilot RCT on adherence, acceptance, and symptom improvement in routine psychosomatic care
summary: Many people with mental or psychosomatic complaints use online self-help programs but frequently discontinue them early. The program "KEN-Online" helps people to better perceive, understand, and express their own emotions. This study examines whether short, personalized, and encouraging messages—created with the help of artificial intelligence and reviewed by trained staff before being sent—help participants use the program more regularly and over a longer period. Adult patients of the psychosomatic clinic receive access to KEN-Online for twelve weeks. Participants are randomly assigned to either receive weekly encouraging messages in addition to the program content or not. Questionnaires and program usage data are used to record how intensively the program is used and how participants are doing.

interventions.name: KEN-Online (psychodynamic online self-help program, 9 modules) over 12 weeks, plus weekly AI-generated motivational feedback messages (human-reviewed)
KEN-Online with identical content over 12 weeks, without AI-generated feedback

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sufficient German language skills to independently understand study information, informed consent, questionnaires, KEN-Online content, and feedback messages
Regular access to an internet-enabled device and ability to use KEN-Online independently
Informed consent provided prior to registration, randomization, and any study-related procedures
Inpatient, day-clinic, or outpatient psychosomatic treatment at the clinic
Exclusion criteria:
Acute suicidality
